questions.stem: What is the correct definition of excretion?

options.text: The breakdown of food molecules in the digestive system
The removal of metabolic waste products from the body
The removal of undigested food from the body
The absorption of nutrients into the bloodstream

questions.explanation: Excretion is specifically the removal of metabolic waste products (substances produced by chemical reactions inside cells) from the body. Removal of undigested food is called egestion, not excretion.

questions.stem: Which organ is responsible for excreting carbon dioxide from the body?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide produced by aerobic respiration in all cells is transported to the lungs via the blood, where it diffuses into the alveoli and is breathed out.

questions.stem: Urea is produced from the breakdown of which type of molecule?
questions.explanation: Urea is produced when excess amino acids (from protein digestion) are deaminated in the liver. The body cannot store excess protein, so the nitrogen-containing amino group must be removed and converted to urea.

questions.stem: Why are faeces NOT considered an excretory product?

options.text: Because the material in faeces was never inside body cells
Because faeces leave through the anus, not the kidneys
Because faeces contain only water and fibre
Because faeces are produced by the large intestine

questions.explanation: Excretory products are metabolic wastes produced inside cells. Faeces consist mainly of undigested food that passed through the gut without ever entering cells, so their removal is called egestion, not excretion.

questions.stem: In which organ does deamination take place?
questions.explanation: Deamination (the removal of the amino group from excess amino acids) occurs in the liver. The ammonia produced is then converted to urea, which is transported to the kidneys for excretion.

questions.stem: What would happen if too much carbon dioxide accumulated in the blood?

options.text: Blood cells would burst due to osmosis
The blood would clot more quickly
The blood would become too acidic, affecting enzyme function
The blood would become too alkaline

questions.explanation: Excess CO2 dissolves in the blood to form carbonic acid, making the blood too acidic. This change in pH affects enzyme function and disrupts homeostasis, which is why CO2 must be continually excreted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the primary function of sweating?

options.text: Removing excess salts from the blood

questions.explanation: Although sweat does contain small amounts of urea, water, and salts, the primary function of sweating is temperature regulation, not excretion. The evaporation of sweat from the skin surface cools the body.
